'''Dewayne Jamal Dedmon''' (born August 12, 1989)<ref>{{cite web|title=MARAUDER MEN'S BASKETBALL 2009–10|url=http://gomarauders.avc.edu/!Stats/09-10%20mgpage/mbbmg/bios.pdf|work=GoMarauders.avc.edu|access-date=January 14, 2014|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100610005624/http://gomarauders.avc.edu/%21Stats/09-10%20mgpage/mbbmg/bios.pdf|archive-date=June 10, 2010}}</ref> is an American former professional [[basketball]] player. Nicknamed "'''the Mechanic'''", he played [[college basketball]] for [[Antelope Valley College]] and [[USC Trojans men's basketball|USC]].

==High school and college career==
===Lancaster and Antelope Valley===
Dedmon attended [[Lancaster High School (Lancaster, California)|Lancaster High School]] in [[Lancaster, California]]. Although tall and athletic, Dedmon did not play high school basketball until his senior year due to his mother's religious objections. His mother, a devout [[Jehovah's Witness]], refused to allow him to play organized basketball, believing it might affect his religious devotion.<ref name="DT">{{cite web|last=Didymus|first=JohnThomas|url=http://www.digitaljournal.com/article/314297|title=Jehovah's Witness college basketball star at life's crossroads|website=Digital Journal|date=November 12, 2011|access-date=January 21, 2017}}</ref> After turning 18, Dedmon, who had already grown to {{height|ft=6|in=8}}, decided to exercise his [[age of majority]] rights and begin playing.<ref name="DT" /> After graduating from Lancaster in 2008, Dedmon attended [[Antelope Valley College]] as a part-time student and did not play basketball during the 2008–09 season.<ref name=bio>{{cite web|url=http://www.usctrojans.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/dedmon_dewayne00.html|title=Dewayne Dedmon Bio|work=usctrojans.com|access-date=January 14, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140116094612/http://www.usctrojans.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/dedmon_dewayne00.html|archive-date=January 16, 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref>

As a freshman at Antelope Valley in 2009–10, Dedmon, who had grown to {{height|ft=7}} tall, helped the Marauders to a 17–14 record while averaging 6.6 points and 7.8 rebounds per game. He also had 46 blocks and tied the school record with seven blocks against Chaffey College on January 22, 2010. Five days later against Victor Valley, he sustained a broken bone in his forehead and an injured nasal cavity when he was hit by an errant elbow. The injury forced Dedmon to miss the final seven regular season games, but he returned for the playoffs where he recorded 5 points and 13 rebounds in his first game back, a win against Miramar College on February 24.<ref name="bio" />

===USC===
On April 14, 2010, Dedmon signed with the [[University of Southern California]] and subsequently redshirted the 2010–11 due to NCAA transfer regulations. He completed one final semester at Antelope Valley but did not play for Marauders in order to keep three full seasons of eligibility. He began practicing with USC in the second semester of 2010–11 when he transferred from Antelope Valley.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.usctrojans.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/041410aaa.html|title=USC Men's Basketball Signs 7-Footer Dedmon|work=usctrojans.com|date=April 14, 2010|access-date=January 14, 2014}}</ref>

As a redshirted sophomore for [[USC Trojans men's basketball|USC]] in 2011–12, Dedmon battled with numerous injuries which curtailed his development but still managed to average 7.6 points and 5.5 rebounds in 20 games (all starts). He led the team with a .551 shooting percentage and made 50 percent or more of his shots in 14 of his 20 starts. He had a season-high 18 points against Oregon on January 19, 2012, and followed that up with eight points and eight rebounds against Oregon State on January 21. Five days later against Colorado, he suffered a season-ending injury with a torn left MCL.<ref name="bio" />
[[File:Dewayne Dedmon (cropped).jpg|thumb|Dedmon with USC in 2012]]
As a junior for USC in 2012–13, Dedmon led the Trojans with 7.0 rebounds to go with 6.7 points in 31 games (29 starts). After struggling to score in the early part of the season, Dedmon had the best stretch of his career toward the beginning of USC's conference slate, averaging 10.8 points, 8.4 rebounds and three blocks per game in a five-game stretch. He tied his career-high of 18 points against Washington on March 6 but was suspended indefinitely on March 12 following a reported Saturday night incident in downtown Spokane between USC players and local bar patrons. USC lost 69–66 to Utah in the opening round of the Pac-12 tournament, two days after the suspensions were announced, with Dedmon and also-suspended senior center James Blasczyk not making the trip to the tournament. The Trojans finished the season with a 14–18 record. Dedmon also averaged 2.1 blocks per game in 2012–13, good for second in the Pac-12 and the sixth-best single season total in USC history, and finished the season ninth in program history with 85 career blocks.<ref>{{cite web|last=Freedman|first=Jacob|url=http://dailytrojan.com/2013/04/24/dedmon-declares-for-2013-nba-draft/|title=Dedmon declares for 2013 NBA draft|work=DailyTrojan.com|date=April 24, 2013|access-date=January 14, 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/dewayne-dedmon-1.html|title=Dewayne Dedmon Stats|work=Sports-Reference.com|access-date=January 14, 2014}}</ref>

On April 24, 2013, Dedmon declared for the [[NBA draft]], forgoing his final year of college eligibility.<ref>{{cite web|last=Pucin|first=Diane|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/la-xpm-2013-apr-24-la-sp-sn-usc-dedmon-nba-20130424-story.html|title=USC's Dewayne Dedmon to leave school early for pros|work=[[Los Angeles Times]]|date=April 24, 2013|access-date=January 14, 2014}}</ref>

==Professional career==

===Golden State Warriors (2013)===
After going undrafted in the [[2013 NBA draft]], Dedmon joined the [[Miami Heat]] for the Orlando Summer League and the [[Dallas Mavericks]] for the Las Vegas Summer League. On September 23, 2013, he signed with the [[Golden State Warriors]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/warriors/news/dedmon-jones-signing-092313|title=Warriors Sign Dewayne Dedmon and Cameron Jones|date=September 23, 2013|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|access-date=November 18, 2013}}</ref> However, he was later waived by Golden State on October 25 after appearing in five preseason games.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/warriors/news/warriors-waive-joe-alexander-seth-curry-and-dewayne-dedmon|title=Warriors Waive Joe Alexander, Seth Curry and Dewayne Dedmon|date=October 25, 2013|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|access-date=November 18, 2013}}</ref> On November 1, he was acquired by the [[Santa Cruz Warriors]] of the [[NBA Development League]] as an affiliate player of Golden State.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/?id=4699994|title=Santa Cruz Warriors Add Seth Curry, Dewayne Dedmon & Joe Alexander|date=November 1, 2013|work=OurSportsCentral.com|access-date=November 29, 2014}}</ref>

On November 18, 2013, Dedmon re-signed with the Golden State Warriors,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/warriors/news/dedmon-signing-20131118|title=Warriors Sign Dewayne Dedmon From D-League's day.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/warriors/news/dedmon-kuzmic-nedovic-20131119|title=Warriors Assign Dedmon, Kuzmic & Nedovic To Santa Cruz Warriors of NBA D-League|date=November 19, ===Philadelphia 76ers (2014)===
On January 14, 2014, Dedmon signed a 10-day contract with the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/sixers/news/sixers-sign-center-dewayne-dedmon-10-day-contract|title=Sixers Sign Center Dewayne Dedmon to 10-Day Contract|date=January 14, 2014|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|access-date=January 14, 2014}}</ref> The next day, he made his debut for the 76ers. In 14 minutes of action, he recorded 7 rebounds and 2 blocks in a 95–92 win over the [[Charlotte Hornets|Charlotte Bobcats]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20140115/CHAPHI/gameinfo.html|title=Notebook: 76ers 95, Bobcats 92|date=January 15, 2014|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|access-date=January 15, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150204131821/http://www.nba.com/games/20140115/CHAPHI/gameinfo.html|archive-date=February 4, 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref> On January 24, he signed a second 10-day contract with the 76ers.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/sixers/news/140124-dedmon|title=Sixers Sign Center Dewayne Dedmon to Second 10-Day Contract|date=January 24, 2014|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|access-date=January 24, 2014}}</ref> After his second 10-day contract expired on February 2, the 76ers parted ways with Dedmon on February 3 after they elected to not sign him for the rest of the season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://basketball.realgm.com/wiretap/231787/76ers-Elect-To-Part-With-Dewayne-Dedmon|title=76ers Elect To Part With Dewayne Dedmon|date=February 3, 2014|work=RealGM.com|access-date=February 3, 2014}}</ref> That same day, he was named to the Futures All-Star roster for the 2014 NBA D-League All-Star Game.<ref>{{cite 12, 2014 }}</ref>

===Orlando Magic (2014–2016)===
On February 25, 2014, Dedmon signed a 10-day contract with the [[Orlando Magic]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/magic/news/magic-sign-dewayne-dedmon-adonis-thomas-10-day-contracts|title=Magic Sign Dewayne Dedmon, Adonis Thomas to 10-Day Contracts|date=February 25, 2014|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|access-date=February 25, 2014}}</ref> He went on to sign a second 10-day contract with the Magic on March 7,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/magic/news/magic-sign-dedmon-thomas-second-10-day-contracts|title=Magic Sign Dedmon, Thomas to Second 10-Day Contracts|date=March 7, 2014|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|access-date=March 7, 2014}}</ref> and then a multi-year deal on March 17.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/magic/news/magic-sign-dedmon-rest-season|title=Magic Sign Dedmon for Rest of Season|date=March 17, 2014|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|access-date=March 17, 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last=Johnson|first=Adam|url=http://www.seadubscentral.com/2014/06/04/nba-d-league-climb-tough-obstacle/|title=NBA D-League Has Yet To Climb Toughest Obstacle|date=June 4, 2014|work=SeaDubsCentral.com|access-date=June 4, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141204155929/http://www.seadubscentral.com/2014/06/04/nba-d-league-climb-tough-obstacle/|archive-date=December 4, 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref>

In July 2014, Dedmon joined the Magic for the [[2014 NBA Summer League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/magic/orlando-magic-announce-roster-southwest-airlines-orlando-pro-summer-league|title=Orlando Magic Announce Roster for Southwest Airlines Orlando Pro Summer League|date=July 1, 2014|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|access-date=July 1, 2014}}</ref> He spent his first full NBA season with the Magic in 2014–15. On March 8, 2015, he had a season-best game with 11 points and 16 rebounds in 103–98 win over the [[Boston Celtics]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/d/dedmode01/gamelog/2015/|title=Dewayne Dedmon 2014–15 Game Log|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=December 7, 2015}}</ref>

On November 7, 2015, Dedmon scored a then career-high 12 points in a 105–97 win over the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20151107/ORLPHI/gameinfo.html|title=Payton helps Magic beat winless 76ers 105–97|date=November 7, 2015|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|access-date=December 7, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160124064219/http://www.nba.com/games/20151107/ORLPHI/gameinfo.html|archive-date=January 24, 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> On March 5, 2016, he was assigned to the [[Erie BayHawks (2008–2017)|Erie BayHawks]], the Magic's [[NBA Development League|D-League]] affiliate.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/orlando-magic-assign-dewayne-dedmon/n-5107774|title=Orlando Magic Assign Dewayne Dedmon|date=March 5, 2016|work=OurSportsCentral.com|access-date=March 5, 2016}}</ref> Two days later, he was recalled by the Magic.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/magics-dewayne-dedmon-recalled-from-d-league/|title=Magic's Dewayne Dedmon: Recalled from D-League|date=March 7, 2016|work=CBSSports.com|access-date=March 12, 2016}}</ref> On March 26, 2016, he recorded a career-high 18 points and a season-high 13 rebounds in 22 minutes as a starter in a 111–89 win over the [[Chicago Bulls]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160326/CHIORL/gameinfo.html|title=Bulls' playoffs hopes dealt blow with 111–89 loss to Magic|date=March 26, 2016|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|access-date=March 26, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160817205502/http://www.nba.com/games/20160326/CHIORL/gameinfo.html|archive-date=August 17, 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===San Antonio Spurs (2016–2017)===
On July 14, 2016, Dedmon signed with the [[San Antonio Spurs]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/spurs/san-antonio-signs-dewayne-dedmon|title=SAN ANTONIO SIGNS DEWAYNE DEDMON|date=July 14, 2016|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|access-date=July 14, 2016}}</ref> He made his debut for the Spurs on October 25, 2016, recording two points, eight rebounds, one steal and two blocks in 16 minutes off the bench in a 129–100 win over the [[Golden State Warriors]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/boxscore?gameId=400899377|title=Spurs vs. Warriors – Box Score|work=ESPN.com|date=October 25, 2016|access-date=February 11, 2017}}</ref> On February 10, 2017, Dedmon had 17 points and 17 rebounds, setting season highs in both categories, to help the Spurs to a 103–92 victory over the [[Detroit Pistons]]. He set a career high in rebounds and finished one point shy of his career high in scoring.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900206|title=Spurs take control at end of 1st half, beat Pistons 103–92|work=ESPN.com|date=February 10, 2017|access-date=February 11, 2017}}</ref>

===Atlanta Hawks (2017–2019)===
On July 21, 2017, Dedmon signed with the [[Atlanta Hawks]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/hawks/news/hawks-sign-big-man-dewayne-dedmon|title=Hawks Sign Big Man Dewayne Dedmon|work=NBA.com|date=July 21, 2017|access-date=July 21, 2017}}</ref> On November 15, 2017, he scored a career-high 20 points and had 14 rebounds in a 126–80 win over the [[Sacramento Kings]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400974955|title=Dedmon, hot-shooting Hawks rout Kings, 126–80|work=ESPN.com|date=November 15, 2017|access-date=November 15, 2017}}</ref> On November 29, 2017, he was ruled out for three-to-six weeks due to a left tibia stress reaction.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/hawks/news/dedmon-miss-3-6-weeks-tibia-injury|title=Dedmon To Miss 3–6 Weeks With Tibia Injury|work=NBA.com|date=November 29, 2017|access-date=December 1, 2017}}</ref> He returned to action on January 8 against the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] on a minutes restriction after missing 19 games.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975344|title=C.J. Williams hits 3 to lift Clippers over Hawks 108–107|work=ESPN.com|date=January 8, 2018|access-date=January 9, 2018}}</ref> On February 11, 2018, Dedmon matched his career high with 20 points and had 13 rebounds in a 118–115 win over the [[Detroit Pistons]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975580|title=Dedmon powers Hawks past Griffin, Pistons 118–115|work=ESPN.com|date=February 11, 2018|access-date=February 11, 2018}}</ref> On March 20, 2018, he had 15 points and 15 rebounds in a 99–94 win over the [[Utah Jazz]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975808|title=Schroder scores career-high 41, Hawks end Jazz win streak|work=ESPN.com|date=March 20, 2018|access-date=March 20, 2018}}</ref>

On December 16, 2018, Dedmon had 24 points and 12 rebounds in a 144–127 loss to the [[Brooklyn Nets]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071117|title=Russell scores 32, Nets beat Hawks 144–127 for 5th straight|work=ESPN.com|date=December 16, 2018|access-date=January 22, 2019}}</ref> On December 26, he had 18 points and a season-best 15 rebounds in a 129–121 loss to the [[Indiana Pacers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071180|title=Young, Sabonis, Evans power Pacers past Hawks 129–121|work=ESPN.com|date=December 26, 2018|access-date=December 27, 2018}}</ref> On January 21, 2019, he scored 24 points and made five of seven 3-pointers in a 122–103 loss to the [[Orlando Magic]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071371|title=Fournier, Vucevic power Magic past Hawks, 122–103|work=ESPN.com|date=January 21, 2019|access-date=January 22, 2019}}</ref> On March 31, he was ruled out for the rest of the season with a left ankle injury.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/atlanta-hawks-injury-update-1|title=Atlanta Hawks Injury Update|work=NBA.com|date=March 31, 2019|access-date=March 31, 2019}}</ref>

===Sacramento Kings (2019–2020)===
On July 8, 2019, the [[Sacramento Kings]] signed Dedmon to a three-year, $40 million contract.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings-sign-dewayne-dedmon |title=Kings Sign Dewayne Dedmon | Sacramento Kings |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=2019-07-09 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191022065854/https://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings-sign-dewayne-dedmon |archive-date=2019-10-22 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Dedmon experienced diminished playing time as [[Richaun Holmes]] and [[Harry Giles (basketball)|Harry Giles]] moved ahead of him in the rotation. On January 2, 2020, the NBA fined Dedmon $50,000 for publicly requesting a trade.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/nba-fines-kings-dewayne-dedmon-50000-for-publicly-requesting-trade/|title=NBA fines Kings' Dewayne Dedmon $50,000 for publicly requesting trade|website=CBSSports.com|date=2 January 2020 |language=en|access-date=January 3, 2020}}</ref>

===Return to Atlanta (2020)===
On February 6, 2020, Dedmon was traded back to Atlanta along with two second round picks, in exchange for [[Jabari Parker]] and [[Alex Len]]. He had a season-high 5 blocks in both his last game before the trade and the first game after, both wins for his team.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/hawks-acquire-dedmon-draftpicks-from-kings-for-len-parker|title=Hawks Acquire Dewayne Dedmon, Draft Picks From Kings in Exchange For Alex Len and Jabari Parker|work=NBA.com|date=February 6, 2020|access-date=February 6, 2020}}</ref>

On November 20, 2020, Dedmon was traded to the [[Detroit Pistons]] in exchange for [[Tony Snell (basketball)|Tony Snell]] and [[Khyri Thomas]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/atlanta-hawks-acquire-tony-snell-detroit-pistons|title=Atlanta Hawks Acquire Tony Snell from Detroit Pistons|work=NBA.com|date=November 20, 2020|access-date=November 20, 2020}}</ref> but was waived four days later.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.freep.com/story/sports/nba/pistons/2020/11/24/detroit-pistons-waive-center-dewayne-dedmon/6415453002/|title=Detroit Pistons finalizing roster after active week of moves, waive center Dewayne Dedmon|website=Detroit Free Press|first=Omari|last=Sankofa II|date=November 24, 2020|access-date=November 26, 2020}}</ref>

=== Miami Heat (2021–2023) ===
On April 8, 2021, Dedmon signed with the [[Miami Heat]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Dewayne Dedmon Signs With HEAT|url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-sign-dewayne-dedmon-040721|date=April 8, 2021|website=NBA.com|access-date=April 8, 2021}}</ref> Dedmon re-signed with the Heat on August 6, 2021, on a one-year veteran's minimum contract.

On July 6, 2022, Dedmon re-signed with the Heat on a two-year, $9 million contract.<ref>{{Cite web |title=HEAT RE-SIGN DEWAYNE DEDMON |url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-resigns-dewayne-dedmon-070622 |access-date=July 9, 2022 |website=NBA}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Report: Miami Heat re-sign Caleb Martin, Dewayne Dedmon |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/miami/news/miami-heat-caleb-martin-three-year-deal/ |access-date=July 9, 2022 |website=CBS News|date=6 July 2022 }}</ref> On January 11, 2023, the Heat suspended Dedmon for one game without pay due to an incident during a game with the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] a day earlier. Dedmon had gotten into an argument with Heat head coach [[Erik Spoelstra]] and threw a massage gun onto the court, resulting in him being ejected from the game.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Heat's Dewayne Dedmon Suspended 1 Game After Hitting Massage Gun onto Court |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/10061412-heats-dewayne-dedmon-suspended-1-game-after-hitting-massage-gun-onto-court |access-date=January 15, 2023 |website=Bleacher Report}}</ref>

On February 7, 2023, Dedmon was traded, alongside a 2028 second-round pick, to the [[San Antonio Spurs]] in exchange for cash considerations.<ref>{{cite web |title=HEAT TRADE DEWAYNE DEDMON |url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-trade-dewayne-dedmon |website=NBA.com |access-date=7 February 2023}}</ref> On February 9, he was waived by the Spurs.

===Return to Philadelphia (2023)===
On February 14, 2023, Dedmon signed with the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Dewayne Dedmon: Quick Facts|url=https://www.nba.com/sixers/news/dewayne-dedmon-bio|website=NBA.com|date=February 14, 2023|access-date=February 14, 2023}}</ref>

===Ontario Clippers (2023–2024)===
On November 17, 2023, Dedmon signed with the [[Ontario Clippers]] of the [[NBA G League]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Rory|last=Maher|title=Dewayne Dedmon Joining Ontario Clippers|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2023/11/dewayne-dedmon-joining-ontario-clippers.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=November 17, 2023|access-date=November 20, 2023}}</ref> 

In the Tip-Off Tournament, Dedmon averaged 5.4 points and 4.6 rebounds in 13 minutes per game. For the regular season, he would play in 14 of the team's first 20 games and averaged 7.4 points and 6.6 rebounds in 16.6 minutes (winning 8 of the 14 games he played in). However, on February 21, 2024, he was waived by the Clippers.<ref>{{cite web|title=2023-2024 Ontario Clippers Transaction History|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/gleague/teams/Ontario-Clippers/65/Transaction_History/2024|website=RealGM.com|access-date=February 21, 2024}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Dedmon is the son of Thomas Dedmon and Gail Lewis, and has two older sisters, Sabrina and Marina. His father died by suicide when Dedmon was just three years old, while his mother is a devout [[Jehovah's Witness]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Ballard|first=Chris|url=https://www.si.com/vault/2011/11/14/106130712/dewayne-dedmons-leap-of-faith|archive-url=https://archive.today/20141130081804/http://www.si.com/vault/2011/11/14/106130712/dewayne-dedmons-leap-of-faith|url-status=dead|archive-date=November 30, 2014|title=Dewayne Dedmon's Leap Of Faith|date=November 14, 2011|work=SI.com|access-date=November 29, 2014}}</ref>

Dedmon married Kayla Dedmon on August 21, 2019. The couple has two children.
